reason: The cohort-to-round-to-release journey is substantially clearer. Explicit authorized cohort selection scopes navigation; older rounds derive their actual cohort; staffing and submitted forms are distinguished from canonical valid evidence. Close grading explains irreversible consequences and reconciles uncertain acknowledgements. Batch release preserves the complete reviewed cohort while filtering, restores focus, and exposes specific round diagnostics. The supplied desktop homepage and synthetic mobile diagnostics show coherent, restrained hierarchy and readable recovery guidance. However, the separately reachable single-outcome release still lacks the acknowledgement and recovery protections of batch release. That inconsistency in a consequential operator journey prevents world-class agreement and warrants a hold. Approved engagement proof, confirmed membership workload and hosted authenticated acceptance also remain absent; local SQL, source and synthetic browser evidence cannot establish successful real operator completion.

findings.evidence: ReleaseButton uses useAction/runAction, which awaits authorizedFetch and response.json without a deadline, accepts every response.ok as success, and reports a lost response as Could not release. Only success or released:true triggers refresh. This button remains rendered in the dossier (applications/[id]/page.tsx:552) and Decisions (hash/page.tsx:414). In contrast, ReleaseAllButton uses full-body deadlines and explicit unknown-result recovery. release-reliability.spec.ts exercises only the batch component.
findings.userImpact: A stalled individual release can remain Releasing indefinitely. A committed release with a lost acknowledgement leaves stale state and generic failure; a malformed successful response can claim confirmed release without a verified receipt.
findings.suggestedFix: Give individual release a bounded complete-response operation, validate its action-specific receipt, and reconcile ambiguous outcomes against authoritative decision state before allowing retry. Add single-release stalled-body, malformed-success and committed-response-loss cases.

notVerified: No hosted Clerk/Supabase/RLS/storage/email or real authenticated cohort, grading and release recovery journey; inspected tests use mocked/intercepted dependencies.
No observed human operator success, screen-reader session, physical iPhone or macOS Safari acceptance. Most full private screens lack supplied final captures.
Board-approved closed-round remediation, original-resume policy resolution and retention operations; diagnostics route to authority but do not supply that policy.
